books.headline: TWO SECONDS LATE
books.hook: you miss the 08:14 by two seconds, a stranger answers your complaint, and you live together for thirty-one years.
books.title: The 08:14
passage: The doors close as you reach them. You mutter, shit. A woman on the platform bench says, professional timing. The next train is nineteen minutes away.
Thirty-one years later you know her key in the lock, the bag on the floor, the fridge before hello. Neither of you agrees on the colour of the bench.
The book keeps the two seconds.
books.aftertaste: Her key turns before hello.

neighbors.difference: You arrive one second earlier and board the train.
You miss the train, but the stranger never answers.

books.headline: ONE SECOND EARLIER
books.title: One Second Earlier
passage: The doors are still open. You step onto the 08:14 and take a seat over the wheels.
The woman on the platform bench remains a stranger. Years pass: work, rent, another address, another person beside you at breakfast.
At the station, you sometimes stand near the same bench without knowing why it matters in another volume.
books.aftertaste: The doors stay open for you.

neighbors.difference: You arrive one second later, miss the train, and meet the stranger.
You miss the train too, but no conversation begins.

books.headline: SAME PLATFORM, NO REPLY
books.title: No Reply
passage: The doors close. You mutter, shit. The woman on the bench hears you and keeps reading.
You both wait nineteen minutes. You sit six feet apart. The next train arrives and you board different carriages.
Thirty-one years later the book still contains both of you. It contains no shared key.
books.aftertaste: The bench holds two strangers.

neighbors.difference: The stranger answers your complaint.
You arrive in time and never wait beside her.

books.headline: FORTY-SEVEN SECONDS
books.hook: your entire professional football career lasts forty-seven seconds, includes one ordinary touch, and is still a professional career.
books.title: Forty-Seven Seconds
passage: At twenty-seven your number goes up. You run on, receive one pass and return it five yards inside.
Forty-seven seconds after you enter, the whistle goes. You never play professionally again.
On Monday you are back on the warehouse rota. Years later the shirt is folded under a box of extension leads.
books.aftertaste: Forty-seven seconds still count.

neighbors.difference: Your professional career lasts forty-six seconds.
Your professional career lasts forty-eight seconds.

books.headline: FORTY-SIX SECONDS
books.title: Forty-Six Seconds
passage: Your number goes up. You run on. The ball starts toward you.
The whistle sounds before it arrives. Forty-six seconds. No legal touch.
On Monday you are back on the same warehouse rota. The same shirt waits in the same box.
books.aftertaste: One second removes the touch.

neighbors.difference: The whistle comes one second later and your touch counts.
The whistle comes two seconds later than here.

books.headline: FORTY-EIGHT SECONDS
books.title: Forty-Eight Seconds
passage: Your number goes up. You run on, return one pass five yards inside, and keep moving.
The whistle goes forty-eight seconds after you enter. Nothing else happens in the extra second.
On Monday you are back on the warehouse rota. The shirt is still folded under extension leads.
books.aftertaste: The extra second contains nothing.

neighbors.difference: Your career is one second shorter.
Your career is two seconds shorter and contains no legal touch.

books.headline: FIVE MINUTES LATER
books.hook: you eat Tuesday's dinner five minutes later than in the adjacent volume, and nothing in the rest of your life changes.
books.title: The Same Dinner
passage: The oven clock reads 19:12 when you sit down. Pasta, grated cheese, water in the same glass.
Wednesday is unchanged. So are the job, the boiler service, the car you replace six years later and the people you call on Sundays.
On that Tuesday, dinner was five minutes later.
books.aftertaste: At 19:12, you rinse the same plate.

neighbors.difference: Dinner is three minutes later instead of five.
Dinner is at the original time, but you use a different fork.

books.headline: THREE MINUTES LATER
books.title: Three Minutes Later
passage: The oven clock reads 19:10 when you sit down. Same pasta, same grated cheese, same glass.
Wednesday is unchanged. So are the years after it.
This volume differs by three minutes.
books.aftertaste: At 19:10, you rinse the same plate.

neighbors.difference: Dinner is five minutes later instead.
Dinner is at the original time, with a different fork.

books.headline: A DIFFERENT FORK
books.title: The Other Fork
passage: You sit down at the original time. The fork in your hand is the other one from the drawer, with the flatter handle.
The dinner, Wednesday and every later year are unchanged.
After washing, the fork goes back into the drawer.
books.aftertaste: The flatter handle dries beside the sink.

neighbors.difference: You use the usual fork, but eat five minutes later.
You use the usual fork, but eat three minutes later.

books.headline: ONE CENTIMETRE LEFT
books.hook: tomorrow at breakfast you set the cup one centimetre farther left, and nothing else in your life changes.
books.title: An Ordinary Thursday
passage: You wake at 07:42, make tea and set the cup one centimetre farther left to clear the toast plate.
The delivery arrives at eleven. You answer a message at four. The boiler engineer confirms Tuesday.
Years pass normally. The centimetre never becomes important.
books.aftertaste: The cup was one centimetre left.

neighbors.difference: The cup moves one millimetre left instead.
The cup stays exactly where it was.

books.headline: ONE MILLIMETRE LEFT
books.title: One Millimetre Left
passage: You wake at 07:42, make tea and set the cup one millimetre farther left.
The delivery, the message, the boiler call and every later year remain the same.
The Library keeps the millimetre.
books.aftertaste: One millimetre has its own volume.

neighbors.difference: The cup moves one centimetre left.
The cup does not move.

books.headline: NO MOVEMENT
books.title: Exactly Where It Was
passage: You wake at 07:42, make tea and set the cup exactly where it stood before.
The delivery arrives at eleven. The message waits until four. Tuesday remains fine for the boiler.
This is the volume where the cup does not move.
books.aftertaste: Exactly where it was.

neighbors.difference: The cup moves one centimetre left.
The cup moves one millimetre left.

books.headline: MINUS ONE FORK
books.hook: you own every object you own now except one ordinary fork, and nothing else in your life is different.
books.title: The Fork You Don't Own
passage: The cutlery drawer contains one fewer fork. There is no gap where it should be and no memory of buying it.
You eat the same meals with the other forks. Nobody asks about the missing one.
The jobs, rooms, people and years remain unchanged.
books.aftertaste: One fork less. A whole volume.

neighbors.difference: The missing object is a teaspoon instead.
The fork exists, but is always kept in a different drawer.

books.headline: MINUS ONE TEASPOON
books.title: The Teaspoon You Don't Own
passage: The cutlery drawer contains every object you know except one teaspoon.
Coffee tastes the same. Desserts are eaten with the others. No one notices an absence.
Everything else in the life matches the adjacent volume.
books.aftertaste: The teaspoon is simply not there.

neighbors.difference: The absent object is a fork.
Nothing is absent, but one fork lives in another drawer.

books.headline: SAME FORK, OTHER DRAWER
books.title: The Other Drawer
passage: You own the fork. It has always been in the drawer beneath the tea towels instead of with the cutlery.
You use it when needed and put it back there without thought.
Nothing else in the book differs.
books.aftertaste: The fork returns to the other drawer.

neighbors.difference: That fork does not exist.
A teaspoon does not exist instead.

books.headline: ONE LETTER DIFFERENT
books.hook: your handwriting is exactly yours, except you have always formed the lowercase g differently.
books.title: Your Other Handwriting
passage: The slant is yours. The pressure is yours. So are the hurried capitals and the way the line rises near the margin.
Only the lowercase g is different: a closed loop where your other volume uses an open one.
School notes, shopping lists and signatures around it remain the same.
books.aftertaste: Every g belongs to this volume.

neighbors.difference: The different letter is t instead of g.
Every letter is the same, but you hold the pen two millimetres closer to the nib.

books.headline: THE T IS DIFFERENT
books.title: Your Other T
passage: Your handwriting matches the adjacent volume in every letter except t.
Here the crossbar sits slightly higher. Nobody comments. You never compare the pages.
Every note you have ever written contains the difference when a t appears.
books.aftertaste: A higher crossbar has its own shelf.

neighbors.difference: The different letter is g.
The letters match, but your pen grip is shifted.

books.headline: THE SAME WORDS, DIFFERENT GRIP
books.title: Two Millimetres Lower
passage: Every word looks exactly as it does in the adjacent volume.
The difference is your hand. You have always held the pen two millimetres closer to the nib.
No written page reveals it.
books.aftertaste: The text is identical. The hand is not.

neighbors.difference: Your pen grip matches, but the letter g is different.
Your pen grip matches, but the letter t is different.

books.headline: THIS SENTENCE
books.hook: this book describes you opening Babel Life and reading this sentence; the adjacent book says you close it one line earlier.
books.title: This One
passage: The book says you open Babel Life, choose this volume and read the sentence about reading it.
It says you reach this paragraph. Nothing in the text makes that a prediction. It is simply a writable account already on the shelf.
The next volume stops one line sooner.
books.aftertaste: This one includes this line.

neighbors.difference: The account ends because you close the book one line earlier.
The account says you read the same sentence twice.

books.headline: ONE LINE EARLIER
books.title: Closed One Line Earlier
passage: The book says you open Babel Life and choose this volume.
It says you read the first paragraph and close it before the sentence that follows.
That sentence still exists in the adjacent volume.
books.aftertaste: This account stops before the next line.

neighbors.difference: You continue one line farther.
You continue and read one sentence twice.

books.headline: THE SAME SENTENCE TWICE
books.title: Read Twice
passage: The book says you open Babel Life and reach this sentence.
Then it says you read the same sentence again.
Everything around the repetition is identical.
books.aftertaste: The second reading has its own volume.

neighbors.difference: You read the sentence once.
You close the book before reaching it.

books.headline: THE SAME TEMPER, 1340
books.hook: you are born in 1340 with the same laugh, the same impatience and completely different things to complain about.
books.title: Your Signature in 1340
passage: You are thirty-eight in 1378. You argue about a boundary stone, wet firewood and a neighbour who borrows tools without returning them.
Your laugh starts the same way it does here. You lose patience at the same speed.
There are no cars, phones or boilers. The temperament remains.
books.aftertaste: The complaint is different. The impatience is not.

neighbors.difference: You are born forty metres away in the neighbouring household.
You are born in 1341 instead of 1340.

books.headline: THE NEXT HOUSEHOLD
books.title: Forty Metres Away
passage: You are born in 1340 forty metres from the house in the adjacent volume.
The same laugh appears over different bread. The same impatience is spent on a different boundary stone.
Your century is unchanged. Only the household moves.
books.aftertaste: Forty metres rewrites the address, not the temper.

neighbors.difference: You are born in the original household.
You are born one year later.

books.headline: ONE YEAR LATER
passage: You are born in the same place with the same laugh and the same quick irritation, one year later.
The wall dispute comes later. The rain does not.
The book needs no reason for choosing 1341.
books.aftertaste: One year has its own life.

neighbors.difference: You are born in 1340.
You are born in 1340, forty metres away.

books.headline: ONE THURSDAY OF BREATHING
books.hook: this book records every breath you take on one Thursday in November, and nothing else.
books.title: The Breathing Book
passage: 06:41:12 — inhale. 06:41:15 — exhale. The entries continue through breakfast, work, stairs, silence and sleep.
No conversation is recorded. No thought is explained. The book gives only breathing and time.
At 23:58:47 there is an exhale. Then the volume ends.
books.aftertaste: A whole book, and only breathing.

neighbors.difference: The fourth breath after waking lasts 0.3 seconds longer.
The book records the following Thursday instead.

books.headline: ONE BREATH LONGER
books.title: Point Three Seconds
passage: The breathing log matches the adjacent volume until the fourth breath after waking.
Here the inhale lasts 0.3 seconds longer.
Every later timestamp returns to the same rhythm.
books.aftertaste: Three tenths of a second fill another volume.

neighbors.difference: The fourth breath has its original duration.
The entire log belongs to the following Thursday.

books.headline: SEVEN DAYS LATER
books.title: The Following Thursday
passage: This book also contains only breaths and timestamps.
They belong to the Thursday one week later. Fourteen intervals differ from the first book.
You could not identify them without placing the volumes side by side.
books.aftertaste: Fourteen differences, none remembered.

neighbors.difference: The breathing log belongs to the previous Thursday.
The previous Thursday differs by only 0.3 seconds in one breath.

books.headline: YOU ARE NOT IN THIS BOOK
books.hook: the two people who are your parents elsewhere never become a couple, live complete lives, and you do not exist.
books.title: Without You
passage: One moves north at twenty-six. The other stays. Each builds a household with someone else.
There is no empty chair, missing photograph or unexplained grief. Nobody in the book is waiting for you.
The life is complete without your absence being noticed.
books.aftertaste: No one in the book misses you.

neighbors.difference: Your parents meet once, speak for two minutes, and never meet again.
Your parents become friends, but never partners.

books.headline: THEY MEET ONCE
books.title: Two Minutes
passage: The two people who are your parents elsewhere meet once in a queue.
They speak for two minutes about the delay. Then they leave in opposite directions.
Both lives continue. You are still not in the book.
books.aftertaste: Two minutes are not enough for you to exist.

neighbors.difference: They never meet at all.
They meet and remain friends.

books.headline: THEY STAY FRIENDS
books.title: Friends Only
passage: They meet, like each other and remain friends for forty years.
There are birthdays, messages, occasional dinners and no shared household.
You never appear. The friendship has no missing person inside it.
books.aftertaste: They know each other. You still do not exist.

neighbors.difference: They never meet.
They meet once and never stay in contact.

books.headline: YOUR EXACT LIFE
books.hook: your exact life is already written from birth to the circumstances of your death.
books.title: Yours
passage: There is a book containing your exact life. Its first page gives the date, time and place of your birth. Then come every home, every meal, every conversation and every day you have forgotten.
One page describes how you reach this sentence. The pages after it contain the time you will wake tomorrow, the first object you will touch and the words you will say before leaving.
The final page gives the exact date, time, place and circumstances of your death.
books.aftertaste: The final page already exists.

neighbors.difference: The same life ends one second later.
Tomorrow you take thirteen steps to the kitchen instead of twelve.

books.headline: ONE SECOND MORE
books.title: One Second More
passage: This volume matches yours from birth until the final day. It contains the same people, the same rooms and every one of the same words.
Only the time printed on the final page changes.
Here, you die one second later.
books.aftertaste: One second needs another volume.

neighbors.difference: The final page ends one second earlier.
Your death does not change, but tomorrow you take one more step.

books.headline: THIRTEEN STEPS
books.title: Thirteen Steps
passage: This volume matches yours in every detail except one tomorrow.
You take thirteen steps from the bed to the kitchen instead of twelve. Nothing else changes: not breakfast, not the years after it, not the final page.
The difference occupies a complete biography.
books.aftertaste: Tomorrow you take thirteen steps.

neighbors.difference: Tomorrow you take twelve steps to the kitchen.
The life matches, except the final page ends one second later.

books.headline: THE FAMILY OPPOSITE
books.hook: you are born into the family across from your home, and your current family simply lives nearby.
books.title: The Door Opposite
passage: There is a book in which you were born into the family living opposite your home. Their parents are your parents. Their children are your siblings.
You grew up in their rooms, ate at their table and learned to speak with their words. The home where you grew up in this life belongs to another family.
Sometimes you pass them on the stairs. You greet them because they live opposite.
books.aftertaste: You greet them because they live opposite.

neighbors.difference: You are born behind every possible door on your street.
Someone else occupies your room in your current family.

books.headline: EVERY DOOR
books.title: Every Door
passage: There is a volume in which you were born behind every door on your street.
In one you are an only child. In another you share a room with three siblings. In another, the person you now call your sister lives two buildings away and never learns your name.
Every door contains a complete childhood.
books.aftertaste: Every door contains a childhood.

neighbors.difference: You are born into the family living opposite your home.
Your current family remains at home, but another child takes your place.

books.headline: YOUR ROOM WITHOUT YOU
books.title: Your Room Without You
passage: In this book your current family lives in the same home. They keep the same jobs, the same meals and almost all the same photographs.
Another child sleeps in your room, takes your place at the table and calls your parents Mum and Dad.
You grow up somewhere else. Neither family notices an absence.
books.aftertaste: Neither family notices an absence.

neighbors.difference: You are born into the family living opposite your home.
You are born behind every possible door on your street.

books.headline: EVERY POSSIBLE SEAT
books.hook: you die in an aircraft accident in every possible seat, at every age and on every route.
books.title: Every Seat
passage: There are books in which you die in an aircraft accident in every possible seat.

For each seat there are every aircraft, airline, airport, destination, route, altitude, delay and weather condition. In some you are six months old. In others seventeen, fifty-two or one hundred and ten.
Every combination needs your whole life before it.
books.aftertaste: Every combination begins with your birth.

neighbors.difference: The same sequence exists for every ordinary way of dying.
The whole life matches until the final minute.

books.headline: EVERY WAY
books.title: Every Way
passage: Then come the books of trains, buses, cars, bicycles and ships.
And the books in which you die walking, swimming, dancing, eating, sleeping or working. For each activity, the age, place, time and people present all change.
In every volume you are born again on the first page.
books.aftertaste: In every volume you are born again.

neighbors.difference: Only the flights, seats, routes and ages change.
The lives remain identical until the final minute.

books.headline: THE SAME FINAL MINUTE
books.title: Until the Final Minute
passage: These books match throughout your life.
Same family. Same body. Same meals, jobs, conversations and journeys. They arrive together at the final minute.
Then each book ends in a different way.
books.aftertaste: Each book ends differently.

neighbors.difference: Every seat, flight, age and route produces another complete life.
The activity, place and people present all change too.

books.headline: LEFT FIRST
books.hook: you put on your left sock first every day of your adult life, and nothing else changes.
books.title: Left First
passage: In this book you put on your left sock first every day of your adult life.
The order changes no conversation, job or relationship. You reach the same places at the same time. You die on the same day.
From eighteen until the end, the left goes first.
books.aftertaste: The left goes first until the end.

neighbors.difference: One Tuesday, at forty-six, you put on the right sock first.
You put on the right sock first every day of your adult life.

books.headline: ONE TUESDAY
books.title: One Tuesday
passage: This volume matches the previous one throughout your life except for one morning.
One Tuesday, at forty-six, you put on your right sock first. You do not notice. Nobody sees.
The rest of the book matches again through its final word.
books.aftertaste: One morning needs another volume.

neighbors.difference: The left sock goes first on that Tuesday too.
The right sock goes first every day, not just once.

books.headline: RIGHT EVERY TIME
books.title: Right Every Time
passage: Here you put on your right sock first from eighteen until your death.
Everything else remains the same: the people you love, the illnesses, the homes, the sentences and the length of your life.
It takes another whole book.
books.aftertaste: It takes another whole book.

neighbors.difference: The left sock goes first every day.
The right goes first on only one Tuesday.

books.headline: ONLY ONE OF YOU CAN REMEMBER
books.hook: every event you share can be remembered by only one of you; when one keeps the memory, the other keeps only the facts.
books.title: One Memory Between Us
passage: Your partner remembers the wedding: the warm room, the missing button, the laugh during the vows. You know those things happened and remember none of them.
You remember a rainy holiday they know only from photographs.
Shared years divide themselves this way. No memory belongs to both.
books.aftertaste: The facts are shared. The memories are not.

neighbors.difference: The wedding memory belongs to you instead.
Telling a shared memory transfers it to the listener.

books.headline: YOU REMEMBER THE WEDDING
books.title: Your Wedding to Keep
passage: In this volume, the wedding belongs to you.
You remember the warm room, missing button and laugh during the vows. Your partner knows the facts and has no image of the day.
The other shared memories divide as before.
books.aftertaste: This time, the wedding stays with you.

neighbors.difference: The wedding memory belongs to your partner.
Memories can move when spoken aloud.

books.headline: SAY IT AND LOSE IT
books.title: Told, Transferred
passage: You remember the rainy holiday until you describe it aloud.
As your partner begins to see the wet balcony and red towel, the images leave you. The facts remain.
From then on, every shared memory can be moved by telling.
books.aftertaste: The listener keeps what the speaker loses.

neighbors.difference: Memories divide but never transfer.
The wedding belongs to you, without transfer.

books.headline: ONE DAY HAPPENED TWICE
books.hook: one ordinary Tuesday in your life occurred twice — you lived it identically both times — and the book records both.
books.title: The Extra Tuesday
passage: The book gives Tuesday 8 October twice.
Both times you wake at 06:47, make tea, miss the same bus, work until five, buy washing powder and watch half a documentary.
Wednesday follows once. You remember one Tuesday.
books.aftertaste: The book keeps both Tuesdays.

neighbors.difference: The second Tuesday differs only because the kettle boils thirty seconds later.
The same Tuesday occurs three times.

books.headline: THIRTY SECONDS LATER
books.title: The Second Kettle
passage: Tuesday 8 October appears twice.
The second copy is identical except the kettle clicks off thirty seconds later. You still miss the same bus.
Wednesday follows once.
books.aftertaste: Thirty seconds appear nowhere else.

neighbors.difference: Both Tuesdays are identical.
Tuesday occurs three times.

books.headline: THREE TUESDAYS
books.title: Tuesday, Tuesday, Tuesday
passage: The book gives Tuesday 8 October three times in succession.
Each copy contains the same tea, missed bus, workday, washing powder and half documentary.
After the third, Wednesday follows.
books.aftertaste: You remember one Tuesday.

neighbors.difference: Tuesday occurs twice.
Tuesday occurs twice with one thirty-second difference.

books.headline: EVERY POSSIBLE BODY
books.hook: you are born with every body you could have had, and each one needs a complete life.
books.title: Every Body
passage: There are books in which you are born on the same day, to the same parents and in the same room, with every body you could have had.
Height, face, sex, voice, strength, mobility and health all change. Every body ages in every way available to it.
None ends with a description. They all need a complete life.
books.aftertaste: Every body reaches its final page.

neighbors.difference: Two bodies differ by only one millimetre of adult height.
Every bodily trait combines with every other one.

books.headline: ONE MILLIMETRE MORE
books.title: One Millimetre
passage: Two of those books match in your family, your face, your health and every event in your life.
In one, your adult height is one millimetre greater. The difference appears as you grow and remains until your death.
A whole volume for that millimetre.
books.aftertaste: A whole volume for that millimetre.

neighbors.difference: Height is only one of all the traits that change.
The millimetre combines with every voice, face, health and family.

books.headline: EVERY COMBINATION
books.title: Every Combination
passage: For every height there are all the voices. For every voice, all the faces. For every face, all the illnesses, injuries, abilities and ways of ageing.
Then each of those bodies lives with every family, in every city, beside every person it could meet.
In one volume you have your present body.
books.aftertaste: In one volume you have this body.

neighbors.difference: Every possible body receives a complete life.
Two of those bodies differ by only one millimetre.

books.headline: 11 JUNE 2047
books.hook: 11 June 2047 is already complete: breakfast, rain, errands, a call and the final light.
books.title: 11 June 2047
passage: There is a book in which you reach 11 June 2047.
You wake at 07:16. You have toast and an orange for breakfast. It rains from 09:08 to 09:41. In the afternoon you buy batteries, collect a shirt and call someone you have not met yet.
At 23:52 you leave a glass on the counter and switch off the kitchen light.
books.aftertaste: At 23:52 you switch off the kitchen light.

neighbors.difference: The rain begins at 09:09 instead of 09:08.
The previous twenty years change, but the day matches word for word.

books.headline: THE RAIN BEGINS AT 09:09
passage: This volume contains the same 11 June 2047.
The breakfast, purchase, shirt, call and glass are identical. Only the rain changes.
It begins at 09:09 instead of 09:08.
books.aftertaste: One minute occupies another complete day.

neighbors.difference: The rain begins at 09:08.
The previous twenty years change completely.

books.headline: ANOTHER TWENTY YEARS, THE SAME DAY
books.title: The Same Day
passage: In this book, the previous twenty years are completely different.
You live in other homes, do other work and know other people. Even so, 11 June 2047 matches word for word: the toast, orange, rain, batteries, shirt and call.
At 23:52 you leave the same glass on the counter.
books.aftertaste: At 23:52, the same glass.

neighbors.difference: The previous twenty years match your present life.
The same day changes only in the minute the rain begins.

books.headline: A ROOM THAT NEVER EXISTED
books.hook: you remember a room you have never entered — its green chair, yellow light and scratched table — more clearly than rooms you lived in.
books.title: The Room You Remember
passage: The room has a green chair by the window, yellow light and a diagonal scratch across the table.
You can remember where the door sticks and the smell from the kitchen beyond it.
No house you have entered contains this room. The memory stays.
books.aftertaste: You remember the scratch most clearly.

neighbors.difference: The same room is remembered, but the scratch runs the other way.
At forty, you walk into the room exactly as remembered.

books.headline: THE SCRATCH RUNS THE OTHER WAY
books.title: The Other Scratch
passage: The green chair, yellow light and sticking door are the same.
Only the scratch differs. Here it runs from the far left corner toward you.
The room still exists only in memory.
books.aftertaste: One scratch separates the memories.

neighbors.difference: The scratch runs in the opposite direction.
The remembered room is eventually found.

books.headline: THE ROOM IS THERE
books.title: Found at Forty
passage: At forty you enter an unfamiliar building and find the green chair, yellow light and scratched table.
The door sticks exactly where you remember it sticking.
Nothing in the book explains why you remembered the room first.
books.aftertaste: The memory arrived before the room.

neighbors.difference: You never find the remembered room.
The remembered scratch runs the other way.

books.headline: THE ADJACENT BOOK SAYS RIGHT
books.hook: this book says you turned left on Wednesday; the adjacent book says right; both say you reached the same desk at 09:04.
books.title: The Wednesday Disagreement
passage: At 08:51 you leave home. At the corner, this volume says left.
You pass the pharmacy, cross at the lights and sit at your desk at 09:04.
The adjacent volume says right. It gives the same arrival time.
books.aftertaste: Both books end the walk at 09:04.

neighbors.difference: You turn right and still arrive at 09:04.
The book says you never leave home and still records you at the desk at 09:04.

books.headline: RIGHT, SAME ARRIVAL
books.title: Turn Right
passage: At 08:51 you leave home. At the corner, this volume says right.
You pass the post box and the narrow shop. At 09:04 you sit at the same desk.
The other book insists you went left.
books.aftertaste: Right also arrives at 09:04.

neighbors.difference: You turn left instead.
You never leave home and are still recorded at the desk.

books.headline: YOU NEVER LEFT HOME
books.title: Still at the Desk
passage: The book says you remain at home all morning.
It also says that at 09:04 you sit at the same office desk described in the other two volumes.
No journey connects the sentences.
books.aftertaste: Home and desk share 09:04.

neighbors.difference: The book gives a left-turn journey to the desk.
The book gives a right-turn journey to the desk.

books.headline: ONE WORD AT FOURTEEN
books.hook: at fourteen you say "perhaps" instead of "probably" in a sentence nobody remembers, and the rest of your life is identical.
books.title: Said Perhaps
passage: Near the school gate someone asks if it will rain before you get home. You say, perhaps.
You walk home, eat the same dinner and forget the exchange.
Nobody remembers the word. The book does.
books.aftertaste: This volume contains perhaps.

neighbors.difference: You say "maybe" instead.
You say "probably"; the other person says "perhaps" in reply.

books.headline: ONE DIFFERENT WORD
books.title: Said Maybe
passage: Near the school gate someone asks if it will rain. You say, maybe.
The same dinner, homework and later life follow.
This volume contains maybe.
books.aftertaste: One word gets another book.

neighbors.difference: You say "perhaps" instead.
You say "probably" and hear "perhaps" in reply.

books.headline: THE WORD MOVES TO THEM
books.title: They Said Perhaps
passage: Near the school gate someone asks if it will rain. You say, probably. They answer, perhaps.
The rest of the exchange disappears from memory.
The same word exists in the book, spoken by the other person.
books.aftertaste: The word changes mouths.

neighbors.difference: You are the one who says "perhaps".
You say "maybe" and receive no reply about the word.

books.headline: EVERY LIVING PERSON
books.hook: you share your life with every person alive today whom it would have been possible to meet.
books.title: Every Living Person
passage: There are books in which you share your life with every person alive today whom it would have been possible to meet.
In some you marry. In others you are friends for sixty years, raise a family, work together or stop speaking.
Many of those people will never enter your present life.
Right now they live somewhere without knowing who you are.
books.aftertaste: Right now they do not know who you are.

neighbors.difference: Every person occupies every possible role in your life.
Every possible relationship combines into complete networks.

books.headline: EVERY ROLE
books.title: Every Role
passage: For every person there are books in which they occupy every possible place in your life.
The same person can be your partner, closest friend, employer, carer, someone who harms you or someone with whom you merely share a queue.
Each role combines again with every number of years the relationship could last.
books.aftertaste: Every role has all its years.

neighbors.difference: Every possible person shares a complete life with you.
Every role combines with every other relationship.

books.headline: THE WHOLE NETWORK
books.title: The Whole Network
passage: Changing one person is not enough.
For every possible partner there are all the possible friends. For every group of friends, all the colleagues, neighbours, doctors, teachers and strangers who could affect you.
Every combination forms a different life around you.
books.aftertaste: Every combination forms another life.

neighbors.difference: Every living person appears in every possible bond with you.
One person occupies every possible role.

books.headline: ONE DRAWER, FIFTY YEARS
books.hook: one kitchen drawer in the house you grew up in stays closed for fifty years, and this book never tells you what is inside.
books.title: The Door You Never Opened
passage: The drawer is under the cutlery. Everyone uses the kitchen. Nobody opens it.
Paint changes, appliances change, people leave and return. The handle gathers the same small scratches.
After fifty years the book ends with the drawer still closed.
books.aftertaste: This volume does not open it.

neighbors.difference: The drawer is opened once in year thirty-seven.
The family never opens it; the new owner does in the first hour.

books.headline: YEAR THIRTY-SEVEN
books.title: Opened Once
passage: For thirty-seven years nobody opens the kitchen drawer.
Then someone pulls it out, looks inside for two seconds and closes it. The book does not say what they saw.
It stays closed for the remaining thirteen years.
books.aftertaste: Two seconds do not reveal the contents.

neighbors.difference: The drawer is never opened.
Only the next owner opens it.

books.headline: OPENED IN THE FIRST HOUR
books.title: The New Owner
passage: Your family leaves the drawer closed for fifty years.
The house is sold. In the first hour, the new owner opens it while looking for a place to put batteries.
This book ends before saying what is inside.
books.aftertaste: Another book contains the answer.

neighbors.difference: Nobody ever opens the drawer.
A family member opens it once in year thirty-seven.

books.headline: ONE THING, THEN ALL OF THEM
books.hook: every city combines with every job, every home and every person with whom you could share it.
books.title: One Thing, Then All of Them
passage: First come the books in which you live in every possible city.
For every city there are all the jobs. For every job, all the homes. For every home, all the people with whom you could share it.
No possibility replaces the one before it. Each combines with all the others.
books.aftertaste: Every possibility combines with the others.

neighbors.difference: Even one Tuesday contains all its possible combinations.
Family, body, language and every other detail all change at once.

books.headline: A SINGLE TUESDAY
books.title: A Single Tuesday
passage: Even if your family, body, home and job stay fixed, every possible Tuesday remains.
Every waking time. Every breakfast. Every route. Every person you could pass. Every word you could say and every word you could leave unsaid.
Then come all the combinations among those differences within a single day.
books.aftertaste: All those differences fit inside one Tuesday.

neighbors.difference: The combination begins with cities, jobs, homes and people.
Every category of your life changes at once.

books.headline: YOUR VOLUME AMONG THEM
books.title: Your Volume Among Them
passage: Now family, body, language, city, home, job, partner, children, health, habits and age at death all change at once.
Every combination divides again for every meal, journey, sentence, gesture, object and second.
Among all those books, one matches you exactly.
books.aftertaste: One matches you exactly.

neighbors.difference: The possibilities combine one category at a time.
The combination is limited to a single Tuesday.
